sentences.text: Sutterella wadsworthensis is a member of the genus Sutterella found in the human intestine; Sutterella species were reported abundant in the duodenum of healthy adults with a decreasing gradient toward the colon.

In laboratory experiments S. wadsworthensis preferably bound to mucus and human extracellular matrix proteins and induced interleukin-8 production in enterocytes, although its pro-inflammatory activity was modest.
Sutterella species have been frequently associated with human diseases such as autism, Down syndrome and inflammatory bowel disease, but the impact of these bacteria on health remains unclear.
In intestinal biopsy samples, Sutterella sequences were found in 12 of 23 children with autism and gastrointestinal dysfunction and in none of 9 children with gastrointestinal dysfunction only.
A study of human faecal samples reported evidence for the existence of S. wadsworthensis in human feces.
